# PAPI — agent install runbook

> PAPI (Persistent Adaptive Project Intelligence) keeps a software project on course while an AI assistant builds it. Every new session starts from zero; PAPI holds the plan, the decisions and the direction across all of them, and gives any MCP-capable AI coding tool structured plan/build/review cycles, decision tracking, and a methodology that compounds cycle over cycle.

**Canonical live version: https://getpapi.ai/llms.txt — fetch that URL if you can.**
It carries the current per-client config snippets (Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code,
Windsurf, Codex, generic MCP) and the full docs map, generated from the live
endpoint so it can never drift. This file is the GitHub-resident copy of the
facts that don't change.

## The two facts that govern every client

1. PAPI is a single REMOTE MCP server at `https://mcp.getpapi.ai/mcp`. There is
   no package to install and no local process to run — add the URL as a
   remote/HTTP MCP server named `papi`.
2. There are two ways to authenticate it, and they differ in whether YOU can
   finish the job. On the DEFAULT bearer path you can: the user gives you a
   connection token and a project id from the Connect panel at
   https://getpapi.ai, you write them into the config as headers, and the server
   is live immediately. On the OAuth path you cannot: adding the server does NOT
   authenticate it, the connection sits at "Needs authentication", and only a
   human can complete a browser sign-in. Prefer the path you can finish. A user
   with no PAPI account signs up at https://getpapi.ai first.

Why bearer is the default (C359): across the whole install history, 41 of 72
attempts registered an OAuth client and then died at the browser hop — the
client opens the system default browser, which usually has no getpapi.ai
session, so the user lands on a login wall mid-install. OAuth still works and is
still supported; it is simply no longer the road we point you down first.

The hosted endpoint above is the default and recommended path. A local stdio
runtime is also supported for advanced setups: `npx @papi-ai/server`,
authenticated with an API key instead of a browser sign-in. See "Local runtime
(advanced)" in [llms-install.md](llms-install.md).

## Connect — Claude Code, the plugin (shortest OAuth path)

Two lines, inside Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add getpapi/papi
/plugin install papi@papi
```

The plugin bundles the remote server config, so there is nothing to copy and
nothing to edit. The human still completes the browser sign-in — which is what
makes this the shortest OAuth route rather than the shortest route overall. If
the user has a connection token, the bearer path below is fewer steps and needs
no browser at all.

Note for agents: plugin-bundled tools are namespaced `mcp__plugin_papi_papi__*`
rather than `mcp__papi__*`. If a hook matcher, permission rule or allowed-tools
list is written against the bare name, it will not fire for a plugin install.

## Connect (generic — every client)

### Default — bearer headers (nothing to hand back)

Ask the USER for two values from the Connect panel at https://getpapi.ai. Never
generate them. Then add a remote/HTTP MCP server named `papi` pointing at
`https://mcp.getpapi.ai/mcp` with these headers:

```
Authorization: Bearer <connection-token>
x-papi-project-id: <project-id>
```

In Claude Code:

```
claude mcp add --transport http papi https://mcp.getpapi.ai/mcp   --header "Authorization: Bearer <connection-token>"   --header "x-papi-project-id: <project-id>"
```

The server is authenticated the moment it is added. Call `orient` and you are
in — there is no second step on this path. The config file now holds a
credential: add it to `.gitignore`.

### Alternative — OAuth (only if the user asks, or the client cannot send headers)

Add the server without headers:

```
claude mcp add --transport http papi https://mcp.getpapi.ai/mcp
```

That command is yours to run. The sign-in that follows is not:

```
+-- HUMAN STEP — do not run this yourself ----------------------------
| Hand this step to the user. Only a person can complete a browser OAuth.
|
| Tell them, in their own Claude Code session, either:
|   - open the  /mcp  panel, choose papi, and pick Authenticate.
|     Works on every version, so lead with this one; or
|   - on Claude Code v2.1.186+, the mcp-login subcommand against the papi
|     server — the four words are:  claude / mcp / login / papi  — which
|     opens the browser directly.
|
| Do NOT run either yourself, and do not retry in a background shell, a
| subshell, or a new terminal process. An agent shell is not a TTY, so the
| OAuth prompt fails with "stdin isn't a terminal, so authentication can't be
| completed here". Retrying escalates the failure, it does not fix it.
|
| They must sign in with the same account they used on getpapi.ai.
+-- ── end human step ── ---------------------------------------------
```

**Multi-project? Pin the project first.** The generic connect binds to your
account's DEFAULT project. If you have (or will create) more than one PAPI
project, that default can resolve to the WRONG one. Pin the target with an
`x-papi-project-id: <project-id>` header — open your project at
https://getpapi.ai, use its Connect panel, and copy the project-scoped config
(it already carries the header). One PAPI project? The generic connect is fine.

Per-client blocks for Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Codex, headless/CI bearer
setup and the local stdio runtime: fetch https://getpapi.ai/llms.txt or read
[llms-install.md](llms-install.md) in this repo.

## Prove the connection

Once the user confirms they signed in, call the `orient` tool. If it returns
cycle details, PAPI is connected. If it fails with an auth error, the browser
sign-in was not completed — send the user back to it; do not retry.

If `orient` returns the WRONG project (a different board than the repo you are
in), the config is missing the `x-papi-project-id` header and PAPI fell back to
your account default — re-copy the project-scoped config from the Connect panel
at https://getpapi.ai and reconnect.

Then run `setup` (brand-new project) or follow the next action `orient` returns.

## Docs map

- https://getpapi.ai/llms.txt — this runbook, live, with config snippets
- https://getpapi.ai/docs/guide/quick-start — zero to first cycle in 5 minutes
- https://getpapi.ai/docs/guide/troubleshooting — fetch FIRST when PAPI seems broken
- https://getpapi.ai/docs/tools — every PAPI MCP tool, parameters and use cases
- https://getpapi.ai/docs/install — human-readable per-tool install guide
- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@papi-ai/server — the MCP server package, for
  stdio / advanced local installs
- https://github.com/getpapi/papi — this repo: docs and issue tracker
